div.head: II Cn 25.1
div.ab: ⁊ gilde man þam teonde his ceapgild; ⁊ fo se hlaford elles to healfum, to healfum þæt hundred.
⁊ gilde man þa[m] teonde his ceapgyld; ⁊ fo se hlaford elles to healfum, to halfan þæt hundred.
Et soluatur repetenti captale suum (solutio sue pecunie); reliquum habeat dominus eius dimidium, hundretus dimidium.
⁊ gylde man ðam teonde his ceapgyld ⁊ fó se hlaford elles to healfum ⁊ to healfum þæt hundred.
And gilde man þam teonde his ceapgild, and fo se hlaford elles to healfum, to healfum þæt hundred.
And they shall pay to the accuser the value of his goods, and the lord shall take half of what remains and the hundred half.
And they shall give to the accuser a single payment equivalent to the market value of his goods, and half of the remainder is to be taken by the landlord and half by the hundred.
Und man zahle [davon] dem Kläger dessen Ersatzgeld, und vom Übrigen greife zur Hälfte der Herr [des Verbrechers], (und B) zur Hälfte die Hundertschaft.
And let the plaintiff be paid [from it] his compensation, and of the rest let the lord [of the criminal] take half, (and, B) the hundred half.
